issues.legal_issue: A sale of a small parcel situated some distance from a large acquired tract is not a reliable basis for valuing the acquired land.
material_facts: The acquisition covered a large tract of land.
The sale relied on by the High Court concerned a much smaller parcel situated about two kilometres from the acquired land.
The acquired land was located on the outskirts of an industrial city and had potential value.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not justified in relying on the sale, and it was excluded from the valuation.
issues.legal_principle: In determining market value in compulsory acquisition, the court must assess what a prudent willing purchaser would offer and must not assume that such a purchaser would pay the rate for a small parcel for a large tract. The Court applied the market-value inquiry in the context of a notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894; it relied on no earlier cases.

rule.if: compulsory_acquisition_case and large_area_acquired and comparable_sale_covers_small_area and comparable_land_is_distant

predicates.compulsory_acquisition_case: The proceeding concerns the determination of compensation for land acquired compulsorily.
predicates.large_area_acquired: A large tract of land was acquired.
predicates.comparable_sale_covers_small_area: The sale relied on as a comparable concerned a much smaller parcel than the acquired tract.
predicates.comparable_land_is_distant: The land in the relied-on sale was situated some distance from the acquired land.

issues.definition: When a compulsory acquisition involves a large tract and the relied-on sale concerns a small, distant parcel, that sale is not a reliable basis for valuing the acquired land.

issues.legal_issue: The market value of acquired land may reflect its potential use, but the valuation of a large tract must account for development costs.
material_facts: The acquired land was waste land that was fit for cultivation and possessed potential value for building purposes.
The land was on the outskirts of an industrial city and was acquired for industrial development.
The acquisition covered a large area.
The Court determined compensation at a net rate after deducting one-third for development charges and allowed statutory benefits on the enhanced compensation.
issues.conclusion: The land's potential value was properly taken into account, but compensation was fixed at a net rate of Rs. 22 per square metre after a one-third deduction for development charges; the claimants were also entitled to statutory benefits on the enhanced compensation.
issues.legal_principle: For compensation under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, market value is assessed by applying the test of what a prudent willing purchaser would offer. The land's potential value may be considered, and the Court deducted an amount for development charges in assessing the net value of the large tract. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.compulsory_acquisition_case: The proceeding concerns the determination of compensation for land acquired compulsorily.
predicates.land_has_potential_value: The acquired land had potential for a more valuable use than its existing condition or use.
predicates.large_area_acquired: A large tract of land was acquired.

issues.definition: When land acquired compulsorily has potential value and the acquisition covers a large tract, market value may reflect that potential while accounting for development costs.
